title: Probability: Classical Probability
seo_title: Probability Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 14)
standard_text: Classical definition of probability; simple problems on finding the probability of an event (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Probability worksheet (NCERT Chapter 14): sure and impossible events, complementary events, dice, coins, bags, playing cards and two dice. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How it works

When all outcomes are equally likely, P(E) = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of outcomes.

0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1. A sure event has probability 1, an impossible event 0. P(not E) = 1 − P(E).

A deck has 52 cards: 4 suits (spades, clubs black; hearts, diamonds red) of 13 cards. Face cards are jacks, queens and kings (12 in all). Two dice give 36 outcomes.

Example

A die is thrown. Find P(prime number).

Primes: 2, 3, 5

3 out of 6

Answer: 1/2

Example

Two dice are thrown. Find P(sum = 8).

(2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2)

5 out of 36

Answer: 5/36

Common mistakes

  • Dividing favourable by unfavourable outcomes. Divide by the total.
  • Counting a card twice (the king of hearts is a king and a heart).
  • Taking the 11 possible sums of two dice as equally likely. Use the 36 ordered pairs.

faq.q: What is the formula for probability in Class 10?
faq.a: P(E) = number of outcomes favourable to E ÷ number of all possible outcomes, when the outcomes are equally likely.
E and not E. Exactly one of them happens, so P(E) + P(not E) = 1.

faq.q: How many face cards are there in a deck of 52 cards?
faq.a: 12: a jack, a queen and a king in each of the 4 suits.

faq.q: How many outcomes are there when two dice are thrown?
faq.a: 36, because each of the 6 outcomes of the first die can pair with each of the 6 outcomes of the second.

items.q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting 8?
items.e: Outcomes: 1 to 6. Favourable: none. P = 0/6 = 0.

items.q: A player says: “A coin has two outcomes, so the probability of a head is 1/2.” Is this correct, and why?
c: Yes, because every event has probability 1/2
No, because the coin can land on its edge
Yes, because the two outcomes are equally likely
No, because it depends on the last toss
items.e: The classical definition needs equally likely outcomes, which a fair coin gives. Yes, because the two outcomes are equally likely.

items.q: The probability of an impossible event is ___.
items.e: An impossible event has probability 0. 0.

items.q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number less than 3?
items.e: Outcomes: 1 to 6. Favourable: 1, 2. P = 2/6 = 1/3.

items.q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting an even number?
items.e: Outcomes: 1 to 6. Favourable: 2, 4, 6. P = 3/6 = 1/2.

items.q: If E and not E are complementary events, P(E) + P(not E) = ___.
items.e: Complementary events together make a sure event. 1.

items.q: A student says: “When I throw a die, I either get a 6 or not, so P(6) = 1/2.” Is this correct?
c: No, because P(6) = 1/6 only on the first throw
No, because the two outcomes are not equally likely
items.e: “6” and “not 6” are not equally likely: P(6) = 1/6. No, because the two outcomes are not equally likely.

items.e: There are 81 such numbers out of 90. P = 9/10.

items.q: An event that has only one outcome of the experiment is called ___.
items.e: An elementary event has exactly one outcome. an elementary event.

items.q: A box has 25 discs numbered 1 to 25. One disc is drawn at random. Find the probability that it shows a prime number.

items.q: A piggy bank has 100 coins of 50 paise, 50 coins of ₹1, 20 coins of ₹2 and 10 coins of ₹5. One is chosen at random. What is the probability of a 50 paise coin?
items.e: 100 of the 180 coins: P = 5/9.

items.q: A game has an arrow that stops on one of 8 equal sectors numbered 1 to 8. One is chosen at random. What is the probability of a number greater than 2?
In a lucky draw there are 5,000 tickets, of which 20 carry a prize. Siddharth buys one ticket. What is the probability that he wins a prize?
items.e: 20 prize tickets out of 5,000: P = 1/250.

items.q: Two coins are tossed together. Find the probability of getting at least one head.
items.e: Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT. Favourable: HH, HT, TH. P = 3/4.

items.q: Two dice are thrown at the same time. Find the probability of getting a sum of 8.
items.e: There are 36 equally likely outcomes, and 5 of them give a sum of 8. P = 5/36 = 5/36.

items.q: Two dice are thrown at the same time. Find the probability of getting a sum of 7.
items.e: There are 36 equally likely outcomes, and 6 of them give a sum of 7. P = 6/36 = 1/6.

items.q: In a lucky draw there are 5,000 tickets, of which 10 carry a prize. Riya buys one ticket. What is the probability that she wins a prize?
items.e: 10 prize tickets out of 5,000: P = 1/500.

items.q: Three coins are tossed together. Find the probability of getting at most one head.
items.e: Outcomes: HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT. Favourable: HTT, THT, TTH, TTT. P = 1/2.

items.q: Two dice are thrown at the same time. Find the probability of getting a sum of at most 4.
items.e: There are 36 equally likely outcomes, and 6 of them give a sum of at most 4. P = 6/36 = 1/6.

items.q: In a lucky draw there are 1,000 tickets, of which 25 carry a prize. Dev buys one ticket. What is the probability that he wins a prize?
items.e: 25 prize tickets out of 1,000: P = 1/40.

items.q: In a lucky draw there are 500 tickets, of which 10 carry a prize. Pooja buys one ticket. What is the probability that she wins a prize?
items.e: 10 prize tickets out of 500: P = 1/50.

items.q: Two dice are thrown at the same time. Find the probability of getting a product of 6.
items.e: There are 36 equally likely outcomes, and 4 of them give a product of 6. P = 4/36 = 1/9.

items.q: A jar has 24 marbles, some green and some blue; the probability of a green marble is 2/3. One is chosen at random. What is the probability of a blue marble?
Two coins are tossed together. Find the probability of getting two heads.
items.e: Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT. Favourable: HH. P = 1/4.

items.q: Two dice are thrown at the same time. Find the probability of getting a doublet (the same number on both).
items.e: There are 36 equally likely outcomes, and 6 of them give a doublet (the same number on both). P = 6/36 = 1/6.

items.q: Two dice are thrown at the same time. Find the probability of getting a sum of 13.
items.e: There are 36 equally likely outcomes, and 0 of them give a sum of 13. P = 0/36 = 0.

items.q: Three coins are tossed together. Find the probability of getting exactly two heads.
items.e: Outcomes: HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT. Favourable: HHT, HTH, THH. P = 3/8.

items.q: Two dice are thrown at the same time. Find the probability of getting a sum of 10.
items.e: There are 36 equally likely outcomes, and 3 of them give a sum of 10. P = 3/36 = 1/12.
